lines.text: Every cancer begins with one cell that stops listening, and keeps on dividing.
Fighting it is slow. One idea, one experiment, one answer at a time. A new medicine can take more than ten years.
In 2024, Anthropic's Dario Amodei wrote an essay asking: what if AI could do science alongside us?
Not one mind, but a country of geniuses in a datacenter, testing thousands of ideas at once.
Searching for molecules that fit exactly where cancer is weak.
Teaching the body's own immune cells to see what they had missed.
He called it the compressed twenty-first century: a hundred years of progress, in perhaps ten.
It is a possibility, not a promise. And if it comes, it will be because scientists, doctors and patients kept going.
